key_insight: SAGE-PINN encodes axisymmetric cylindrical geometry directly into a PINN to remove the axis singularity and enforce mass conservation by design.
engineering_relevance: This enables mesh-free surrogate simulation of coupled flow and heat transfer in cylindrical systems such as stenosed arteries across varying buoyancy and advection regimes.
method: Use parity-preserving variable s = r^2 and a modified stream-function to eliminate explicit 1/r singular terms.
Enforce boundary conditions exactly with boundary-fitted analytical ansätze.
Stabilize training with staged momentum-thermal-joint optimization, residual normalization, and Péclet/Richardson continuation.
evidence_signal: Validated against finite-element reference solutions for steady nanofluid flow and heat transfer, achieving about 1.6% relative L2 error in axial velocity and 9.1% in temperature over the central operating range, with mass conservation at single-precision round-off.
watch_item: Accuracy degrades in extreme regimes, especially strongly buoyancy-influenced slow flow and highly advection-dominated heat transfer.
paper_title: SAGE-PINN: A Singularity-free Axisymmetric Geometry-Encoded Physics-Informed Neural Network for Axisymmetric Multiphysics Flow in Cylindrical Coordinates
